comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C15-C18. Both evaluations support the conclusion that untrained bees cannot discriminate string connectivity. OpenEval provides detailed statistical justification (48%, p=0.83, n=21), while peer reviewer explicitly affirms 'bees do not have an untrained understanding of the function of the string.'

Perfect agreement on claims C19-C24, C51, C54, C86. Both evaluations support that trained bees prefer connected strings. OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence (p<0.001, n=18) and convergence of behavioral measures, while peer reviewer affirms 'with training, bees have a preference for unbroken over broken string.'

Perfect agreement on claims C25-C31, C52, C87, C88. Both evaluations support color generalization findings. OpenEval notes reduced first-choice accuracy but maintained discrimination (p<0.001-0.05), while peer reviewer explicitly states 'bees readily generalize across different colors.'

Perfect agreement on claims C33-C35. Both evaluations support that bees maintained discrimination despite restricted visual access during training. OpenEval provides statistical details (n=15, p<0.001) and notes interpretive complications, while peer reviewer accepts findings without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C36-C38, C66, C89. Both evaluations support that eliminating visual access abolished discrimination. OpenEval raises concerns about high exclusion rate (55%) and potential selection bias, while peer reviewer accepts the interpretation that visual cues are essential without noting methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C40-C47, C90. Both evaluations support that coiling strings eliminated discrimination. OpenEval provides detailed statistical evidence (n=19-20) supporting image-matching hypothesis, while peer reviewer states 'bees showed no preference' in experiments 7 and 8.

Perfect agreement on claims C39, C53, C62-C64, C67, C81, C85, C91. Both evaluations strongly support the main conclusion of image-matching over causal understanding. OpenEval synthesizes evidence across all nine experiments, while peer reviewer explicitly affirms 'convincing evidence that bumblebees lack causal understanding' and support for image-matching.

Perfect agreement on claims C82-C84. Both evaluations support the measured conclusion acknowledging limits of interpretation. OpenEval praises the appropriately cautious framing, while peer reviewer accepts the negative finding and the caveat about generalization to other paradigms.

Substantial overlap on latency findings (claims C48-C50, C68-C69). OpenEval explicitly evaluates these claims as supported but notes the interpretation is speculative and secondary. Peer reviewer does not explicitly comment on latency data but implicitly accepts findings without raising concerns.
OpenEval evaluates background and context claims C1-C11, C32 as supported by established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory claims.
OpenEval evaluates knowledge gap and rationale claims C12-C14, C55 as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these framing claims.

OpenEval evaluates comparative context and discussion claims C56-C61, C70-C80 as supported, noting some speculation about bumblebee visual strategies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological claims C92-C96 as uncertain, raising concerns about high exclusion rate (55%) in Experiment 7 and potential selection bias. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these methodological concerns.
